Interactive model appears here after loading. Rendered views are available below even without WebGL2.

Drag to orbit · right-drag to pan · scroll or pinch to zoom. Camera buttons return to recorded viewpoints. Large models may take time to load; only the selected model downloads.

The 3D browser format retains all Gaussian positions, shapes and opacities, with quantized positions, sizes, rotations and base colors (no view-dependent spherical harmonics). Rendered views use the full trained appearance at up to 960 pixels on the long edge. Original full-quality checkpoints and PLY files remain local. Holes, fog and floaters are real limitations of this first attempt; independently trained components are not aligned.

Gaussian splatting · Attempt 01

5 TRAINING RUNS COMPLETE / RTX 4090

Each native-resolution COLMAP dataset was trained independently with gsplat 1.5.3 for 30,000 steps. The separate 8× component is also retained as its own model.

Quality review required. A sampled 2× validation view has severe washed-out and occluded areas. Completed training does not establish a faithful room reconstruction. All four COLMAP pipelines are complete, including full-resolution fusion and meshing.

Held-out validation scores: higher PSNR/SSIM and lower LPIPS generally indicate closer image agreement. Different resolutions and held-out frame sets prevent a direct ranking. These are image-similarity scores, not room dimensions or geometry accuracy.

Settings and local outputs

CUDA device 0 · default strategy · packed rasterization · data factor 1 · 7,000/30,000-step evaluations and checkpoints · separate 100-step smoke test passed.

Files remain in gsplat_local/runs/<dataset>/: ckpts/ckpt_29999_rank0.pt, ply/point_cloud_29999.ply, and renders/val_step29999_*.png. The saved validation images show source and predicted views side by side. These files are local; this section reports aggregate results only.

Use the Gaussian viewer above for trained models. The other geometry viewers show COLMAP point clouds.
